newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Lower House approves re-election bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Lower House approves re-election bill.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies gave a second approval on Tuesday to a constitutional amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year.

The amendment was approved by 368 deputies, 60 more than the three-fifths majority required. One hundred and twelve deputies voted against and five abstained, Lower House president deputy Michel Temer said.
The amendment, that also allows state governors and mayors to seek a second term in office, must now advance to the Senate where it will also require two rounds of voting.

The Lower House is also due to vote on an amendment floated by the left-wing Worker's Party (PT) but which also has government support spelling out that executive office holders will be limited to two consecutive terms.
Up until now drafts of the re-election amendment bill have not specified how many times executive office holders will be allowed to run for the same post.

Government officials have said they intend to begin preparing for a first vote on a civil service reform bill, once re-election cleared the Chamber of Deputies. They aim to put the bill, which would reduce public spending on payrolls, to both its Lower House votes by the end of March.
